TunnelMetadataInfo: This tunnel is managed by the WireGuard app. Only group assignment and notes can be edited here - connection settings are stored in the WireGuard profile.
TunnelDialogNotesHint: Optional. Shown as a tooltip on the tunnel name.
TunnelDialogDataCapsHint: Each period shows a usage bar or ring on the tunnel's row. With 'Use history' it measures against this tunnel's typical usage (informational only). Untick it to set your own cap in MB: MasselGUARD then warns (log, tray, row highlight) and can disconnect ('Kill at cap') when usage crosses it. 0 = no cap. Usage is estimated from connection history and is not exact - MasselGUARD is not responsible for inaccurate reporting, or for tunnels being disconnected (or not) as a result.
SplitSectionHint: Choose which destination IP ranges go through this tunnel. Local tunnels only.
SplitModeOff: Off - route everything through the tunnel
SplitModeExclude: Exclude these ranges (full tunnel except the list)
SplitModeInclude: Only these ranges (everything else bypasses the tunnel)
SplitRangesHint: One per line, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24 or 10.0.0.5. IPv4 and IPv6 supported.
SplitInvalidRange: "{0}" is not a valid IP range. Use CIDR notation like 192.168.1.0/24.
CapConnectConfirmMsg: You have reached the data cap for "{0}" ({1} of {2}). Connect anyway and ignore the limit?
TunnelScriptsInfo: Run a .bat or .ps1 file (or embed a script inline) before or after a tunnel connects or disconnects. Scripts run as the current user. Exit code 0 = success.
SettingsDefaultActionInfo: Choose what happens when you connect to a network that has no matching rule.
SettingsOpenWifiInfo: Automatically activates a tunnel whenever you connect to an open (passwordless) WiFi network - before any rule is evaluated. This protects you on public hotspots.
SettingsClearLogOnStartTip: When off, the log is kept in a file across restarts (trimmed to the max size below).
SettingsMaxLogSizeTip: Oldest lines are dropped once the file passes this size. 0 = unlimited. Applies from the next start.
SettingsDnsLeakInfo: On a split-tunnel WireGuard connection, Windows can send DNS queries out adapters other than the tunnel, leaking them to the local Wi-Fi/router resolver instead of the tunnel resolver - so DNS-based filtering and ad-blocking stop working. The two machine-wide Windows policies below close that gap; for full protection, disable both. Local network access is unaffected.
SettingsDnsLeakSmartDesc: Windows sends each DNS query out all active adapters at once and takes the first answer. Disable to keep DNS on the tunnel resolver.
SettingsDnsLeakParallelDesc: Windows looks up IPv4 (A) and IPv6 (AAAA) at the same time, which can leak the AAAA query. Disable to query them sequentially (slightly slower).
SettingsDnsLeakWarnDesc: How to alert you when an active tunnel may be leaking DNS and protection is off. Turn all three off to disable. (The log and tray alerts stay silent once smart name resolution is disabled above.)
SettingsDnsLeakStatusOff: Enabled - Windows default (DNS may leak on split tunnels).
SettingsDnsLeakReboot: Reconnect your tunnel for changes to take effect - a reboot guarantees it. These are global Windows settings, not per-tunnel.
SettingsDnsLeakAppliedMsg: DNS setting updated. Reconnect your tunnel (or reboot) for it to fully take effect.
TooltipQuickConnect: Open a .conf file and connect instantly - no import needed
SettingsSuppressUpdatePrompt: Don't ask to update the installed version at startup
WizardWelcomeBody:
MasselGUARD automatically activates WireGuard tunnels based on your WiFi network.

This wizard takes about a minute. You can re-run it anytime from Settings.
WizardDoneBody: MasselGUARD is configured and ready. Add tunnels, DNS profiles and automation rules from the main window.
WizardRulesBody: Rules decide which tunnel and DNS to apply when your network changes. You set them up in Settings after this wizard.
WizardManualBody: MasselGUARD can switch your tunnel and DNS automatically based on the network you join.

SettingsAutoReconnectModeDesc: Choose when auto-reconnect is active. Per tunnel = each tunnel controls its own setting. Always = every tunnel reconnects regardless of the per-tunnel toggle.
SettingsKillSwitchModeDesc: Choose when the kill switch is active. Per tunnel = each tunnel controls its own setting. Always = kill switch is on for every tunnel, ignoring the per-tunnel toggle.
SettingsConfigValidationDesc: Pre-flight validation checks WireGuard config files for errors (invalid IPs, missing keys, bad CIDRs) before connecting. Disable globally only as a last resort - invalid configs will still fail, just with a less clear error.

BtnDnsRevertDefaultTip: Undo the active DNS profile - hand DNS back to the tunnel when one is connected, otherwise the system default.
DnsProfileDohNote: Windows 11 auto-upgrades to encrypted DNS once the resolver's IP has a DoH template. Well-known resolvers are built in; custom ones need a template above.

SettingsDnsEnableDesc: Applies the DNS profile of the matching automation rule on each network, even when no tunnel is active. Off: DNS only changes when you turn a profile on yourself. Needs the DNS feature to be on (General > Feature settings).
SettingsDnsInfo: Choose which DNS resolver applies on each network. A connected tunnel's own DNS takes over unless you manually enable a profile.
SettingsDnsProfilesInfo: Define the DNS resolvers you can assign to networks and rules.
TesterInfo: Runs live tests and shows a detailed debug log. The WireGuard test connects an available local tunnel, confirms the peer handshake, then disconnects. The DNS test creates a temporary test profile, applies it to the active interface, reads the resolvers back, then restores your previous settings. A local tunnel must be configured for the connection test.
SysDiagInfo: Opens a read-only overview of every network adapter, the active tunnels, and the DNS servers in use.
TesterSelectMode: Select at least one test to run.
SettingsStartMinimizedDesc: Launch straight to the system tray without showing the main window.
WizTbShowLog: Show the activity log show/hide button
WizTbShieldDesc: A shield button in the title bar that shows or hides the tunnels section.
WizTbGlobeDesc: A globe button in the title bar that shows or hides the DNS profiles section.
WizTbChartDesc: A bar-chart button in the title bar that shows or hides the charts panel.
WizTbMenuDesc: A menu button in the title bar that shows or hides the activity log.
WizTbDisDns: Hiding also turns the DNS feature off
WizTbDisTunnelsDesc: Off = hide only - tunnels keep running, just the section is hidden. On = the button also turns the tunnel feature off.
WizTbDisDnsDesc: Off = hide only: DNS keeps working, just the section is hidden. On = the button also turns the whole DNS feature off.
WizTbDisWifiDesc: Off = hide the panel only: rules keep working. On = the button also switches to Manual mode (no automation).
SettingsConfirmOnExitDesc: When active tunnels are running, ask before disconnecting them on exit. When off, tunnels are disconnected silently.
SettingsWgOffDesc: Turn on the WireGuard feature to configure tunnel groups, auto-reconnect, kill switch and the other tunnel settings.
SettingsDnsOffDesc: Turn on the DNS feature to configure per-network resolvers, DNS profiles and leak protection.
SettingsThemeRepoDesc: GitHub repository the theme browser (Appearance → Download themes…) downloads from. Leave blank to use the official MasselGUARD themes repository. Themes install per-user into %APPDATA%\MasselGUARD\themes.
SettingsThemeRepoResetTip: Reset to the official MasselGUARD themes repository
SettingsFontPreviewApplyTip: Apply this font to the whole interface for 10 s
WizFeatureTitle: What will you use MasselGUARD for?
WizFeatureDesc: Pick the features you want. You can change this later in Settings - this just hides the parts you don't need.
WizFeatureVpnDesc: Manage WireGuard tunnels, with kill switch, split tunneling and data-usage tracking.
WizFeatureDnsDesc: Switch DNS resolvers (plain or encrypted DoH) per network, with or without a tunnel.
WizAppearanceDesc: Choose light or dark mode and a theme. Everything is editable later in Settings → Appearance.
WizStartupDesc: Choose how MasselGUARD is installed and how it launches.
WizStartMinDesc: Launch hidden in the system tray instead of opening the window.
WizConfirmExitDesc: Ask before disconnecting active tunnels when closing the app.
WizWgDesc: Defaults for how tunnels reconnect and protect you. Every tunnel can override these individually later.
WizArDesc: When a tunnel drops unexpectedly, try to bring it back automatically.
WizKsDesc: Block all traffic if a tunnel drops, so nothing leaks outside the VPN.
WizDnsDesc: Apply a DNS resolver per network - even with no tunnel active. Turn it on here, then create profiles and rules in Settings → DNS.
WizDnsHowDesc: A DNS profile is a set of resolvers (e.g. Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, or an encrypted DoH server). WiFi rules pick which profile applies on each network; a default covers the rest. While a tunnel is connected, its own DNS takes over automatically.
WizDnsEnableDesc: Off = MasselGUARD never changes your DNS on its own. On = DNS profiles are applied per network by your automation rules.
WizNotifDesc: Tray toasts when automation switches things, and what gets recorded to history.
WizRecDnsDesc: Save which DNS profile/resolver was active over time (drawn as the DNS band in the charts).
MainTbDnsTip: Show / hide the DNS profiles section
MainEmptyStateBody: You've hidden or disabled every section - you're not using MasselGUARD to its full potential. 🙂 Turn one back on from the title-bar buttons or Settings.
SettingsFeaturesIntro: Turn feature areas on or off, choose what their title-bar button does, and hide any button you don't want.
FeatDnsDesc: DNS profiles, the DNS buttons and per-network DNS. Turn off to remove everything DNS from MasselGUARD.
FeatAutoDesc: Rules that switch the tunnel and DNS for you when the network changes (Wi-Fi or cable). Turn off to switch everything by hand.
FeatLogDesc: Live event log. When disabled nothing is written to the log.
FeatChartsDesc: Records connection / WiFi / DNS history and draws the timeline, data-usage and DNS charts. When disabled nothing is recorded.
SettingsAutoOffDesc: Turn on Automation to configure WiFi rules, the default action and trusted networks.
MainLogExpandTip: Open the activity log in a larger window

TestRuleTip: Check whether this rule's requirements are met right now and write the result to the activity log.
RuleMatchValueSubnet: Subnet(s) in CIDR notation, comma-separated (e.g. 10.20.0.0/16, fd00:1::/64)
RuleMatchHintSsid: Matches any network with this Wi-Fi name. Names like "Guest" are reused by many networks.
RuleMatchHintSuffix: Matches a network that hands out this DNS suffix, over cable or Wi-Fi. Subdomains match too.
RuleMatchHintMac: Best for a network you own: the MAC address of its router. It stays the same across SSIDs and cable.
RuleMatchHintSubnet: Last resort: many networks share 192.168.1.0/24. Prefer gateway MAC or DNS suffix. List an IPv4 and an IPv6 subnet to match either.
RuleFetchTip: Read the value from a network that is connected right now.
RuleFetchNone: None of the connected networks has a value for this match type right now.
RuleValueRequired: Please enter a value to match.
RuleMacInvalid: That is not a valid MAC address (12 hex digits, for example aa:bb:cc:00:11:22).
RuleSubnetInvalid: That is not a valid subnet list (for example 10.20.0.0/16, fd00:1::/64).
SettingsPrimaryNetworkHint: When Wi-Fi and a cable are both connected, the primary network decides which tunnel is used. DNS rules are applied to every connected adapter.
SettingsTrustedPrefixHint: Besides Wi-Fi names, an entry can be suffix:corp.example.com, mac:aa:bb:cc:00:11:22 or subnet:10.20.0.0/16. Use Fetch to add a connected network.
WizardNetworkBody: Rules can match a Wi-Fi name, or the DNS suffix, gateway MAC or subnet of any network, including a cable. When Wi-Fi and a cable are both connected, the primary network decides the tunnel. Match priority and the primary network are set in Settings > Automation.
SettingsRuleOrderHint: When several network rules match the current network, the first one in the Automation rules list (top-down) wins. Drag rows in the list to change the order.
TestAdvTip: Describe a network (or fetch the current one) and see which rule would be triggered, with the reasoning.
TestAdvIntro: Describe a network, or fetch the current one, and see which rule the automation would pick and why. Nothing is connected or changed.
TestAdvFetchNone: There is no connected network to fetch from.
RuleCondHint: All conditions must hold on the same network. Use 'is not' to exclude a network. For OR, add another rule: the first matching row in the table wins.
RuleColOrderTip: Rule order: when several network rules match, the lowest number wins. Drag rows to change it. Sorting the table does not change this number.
RuleMatchHintConnType: Matches how the network is connected: over Wi-Fi or over a cable (Ethernet). Combine it with another condition, for example a router that only counts over Wi-Fi.
RuleMatchHintAdapterName: The adapter's name in Windows, such as Ethernet, Ethernet 2 or Wi-Fi (the Windows counterpart of Linux eth0). Exact match. Several names separated by commas match any of them. Windows can rename an adapter, for example when a dock lands on another port.
RuleMatchHintAdapterDesc: Part of the adapter's hardware description, such as Realtek or USB GbE. Handy to tell a dock's network card from the built-in one. Matches when the description contains your text. Several texts separated by commas match any of them.
RuleMatchHintAdapterMac: The adapter's own hardware address (not the router's): the most stable way to name one specific network card. Several addresses separated by commas match any of them. Specific to this PC, so it does not carry over to another machine.
FetchOtherAdapters: Other adapters on this PC (not connected)
FetchShiftHint: Shift+click adds to the list instead of replacing it
SettingsSimpleWifiDesc: Classic behaviour for people who only use Wi-Fi names. Only Wi-Fi networks are considered, so a docked cable never takes over, and only rules that match a single Wi-Fi name (SSID) are used. Rules with other conditions stay in the list, dimmed, but do not fire. The rule dialog then offers only the SSID. DNS rules follow the same limits.
RuleSimpleModeNote: Simple Wi-Fi mode is on: a rule is just a Wi-Fi name (SSID). Turn it off in Settings > Automation for more options.
SettingsNetNotifyDesc: Show a pop-up when the network you are on changes: the new network, whether it is open, the DNS in use, whether a tunnel is up and which automation, if any, applied. 'Only when no rule matched' skips networks that an automation already handled.
SettingsGroupsDesc: Groups sort your tunnels into tabs on the main window, for example Work and Personal. Put a tunnel in a group from its own editor. 👁 shows or hides a group's tab, ⭐ marks the group that is open on startup, the colour tints the group's tab, and the arrows change the tab order. Tunnels without a group appear under Uncategorized.
SettingsGroupNewTip: Name for a new group, then press Add
GroupDeleteTip: Delete this group (its tunnels stay and move to Uncategorized)
FooterDnsTip:
DNS servers in use right now (the active tunnel's, otherwise the primary network's):
{0}
HistoryRefreshDesc: The chart is rebuilt from scratch on every refresh. Longer intervals use less CPU and memory. Resizing or changing the range always redraws at once. Values are kept within the limits shown.
HistoryRefreshIdle: Seconds between refreshes while nothing is connected (5-60)
HistoryRefreshActive: Seconds between refreshes while a tunnel is connected (1-10)
SettingsTrimTray: Free memory while hidden in the tray
SettingsTrimTrayDesc: When the window is closed to the tray, MasselGUARD compacts its memory and gives the unused part back to Windows. The first redraw after reopening can be a little slower.
DnsTempFooterTip: Timed DNS override running. Click to stop it and go back to automatic.
DnsBypassBadgeTip: Bypass profile: the quick bypass action (tray menu, Ctrl+Alt+D) uses this one
DnsBypassNoneSet: No bypass profile is marked yet. Right-click a DNS profile and choose 'Mark as bypass profile', or pick one in Settings > DNS.
SettingsDnsBypassTip: The resolver the quick bypass action uses, for example Google DNS to get past a DNS ad-block. Used for a timed override from the tray menu, Ctrl+Alt+D, or Shift+Enter in the DNS list.
SettingsDnsTempDesc: Offer 'use this profile for 10 seconds / 1 / 5 / 15 minutes' (right-click a profile, tray DNS menu, Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Alt+D). The override ends by itself and returns to automatic.
PresetItemDnsTempOverride: Timed DNS override (use a profile for a short time)
DnsBypassFooterTip: Bypass profile. Click to use it for a short time (press again to stop). Change the length in the DNS list's right-click menu.
DnsBypassFooterTipOff: Bypass profile. The timed DNS override is switched off in Settings > DNS.
SettingsDnsShellDesc: Add 'DNS bypass' to Windows Explorer's right-click menu (desktop and folders): use the bypass profile for 10 seconds / 1 / 5 / 15 minutes without opening MasselGUARD. MasselGUARD must be running. On Windows 11 it appears under 'Show more options'.
RulePrefillNote: Added from the network you are on: {0}. Use + Add condition to combine it with more (gateway MAC, subnet, ...).
RuleNetMenuNoDetails: No details to identify this network
RuleNetMenuSimpleWired: Wired networks are not used in Simple Wi-Fi mode
RuleNetMenuTip: Create a rule from a connected network
RuleShadowNote: Rule "{0}" above also matches this network and wins. Drag the new rule above it to change that.
SettingsDnsShortcutTip: Click the box and press the keys you want, for example Ctrl+Alt+D. It needs Ctrl, Alt or Win plus one key. Clear removes the shortcut. The value is stored in config.json as BypassShortcut.
SettingsDnsShortcutGlobalDesc: Also register the shortcut system-wide, so it works in any program and while MasselGUARD is hidden in the tray. If another program already uses it, it only works while MasselGUARD has focus.
PresetItemBypassShortcutGlobal: Register the DNS bypass shortcut system-wide
SettingsServiceDesc: Runs the privileged part of MasselGUARD (tunnels, DNS, kill switch) as a Windows service, so the app itself needs fewer administrator prompts. Installing asks for administrator approval once.
ServiceStatusRestart: Running - restart MasselGUARD to use it.
InstallServicePrompt: Also install the MasselGUARD service? It lets MasselGUARD manage tunnels, DNS and the kill switch without elevating the app itself. You can remove it later in Settings > Startup.
ServiceNeedsInstall: The service needs MasselGUARD installed in a local folder (not OneDrive or a network path). Install MasselGUARD now? The service is set up as part of the installation.
ServiceInstallDone: The service is installed. Restart MasselGUARD now to use it?
ServiceRemoveConfirm: Remove the MasselGUARD service? MasselGUARD goes back to elevating itself.
ServiceRemoveDone: The service was removed. Restart MasselGUARD now to switch back?
ElevationNeededMsg: This action needs administrator rights. Restart MasselGUARD as administrator now? Afterwards, repeat the action.
SettingsHeadlessLabel: Keep automation running when MasselGUARD is closed
SettingsHeadlessDesc: With the MasselGUARD service installed, the service keeps applying your network rules (connect or disconnect a tunnel, switch DNS) while the window is closed, for example before you sign in. It works from the last settings MasselGUARD sent to the service and hands control back as soon as a window is open again. Closing MasselGUARD then leaves your tunnels and the kill switch in place. Off by default.
SettingsHeadlessNeedsService: This needs the MasselGUARD service. Install it first (Settings > Startup > Background service).
PresetItemHeadlessAutomation: Automation keeps running in the service when the window is closed
SettingsHeadlessLimits: Not done by the service while the window is closed: history entries, notifications, data caps, schedule rules and your pre/post connect scripts.
ToastBypassUntil: Until {0}, then back to automatic DNS
SettingsBypassSecondsTip: How long the quick bypass stays on when no length is chosen: the keyboard shortcut, the tray and footer item, Shift+Enter on a profile and the right-click menu without a length. 5 to 3600 seconds. Press the shortcut again to stop it earlier.
PresetItemBypassDefaultSeconds: Default length of the DNS bypass
DnsPickSearchHint: Search by name, provider or feature
DnsPickEncOnly: Answers encrypted queries only; plain DNS is refused.
DnsPickNoSelection: Select a server to see what it does.
DnsPickSourceOnline: List is up to date: {0} servers
DnsPickRefreshFailed: Could not update the list ({0}). The previous list stays in use.
DnsPickInputError: Use only letters, digits, - and _ (up to 64 characters).
SettingsDnsListRepoDesc: The GitHub repository (https://github.com/owner/repo) whose index.json and servers folder provide the list in Browse DNS servers. Only change this to use your own copy of the list.
DnsPickTestTip: Sends a few DNS queries from this PC to the listed servers and shows how fast each one answers. Only the servers in the current list are asked.
DnsPickLegend: The bar at the left of a row shows what happens: grey = stays in your list, accent colour = will be added, red = will be removed. Untick a server that is in your list to remove its profile.
DnsPickTestNameTip: The host name every server is asked to resolve. Change it to test with a name you care about (a server that blocks that name will show no answer).
DnsPickTestNameBad: Enter a plain host name, for example masselink.net.
DnsPickParamMissing: Fill in the field of {0} first (letters, digits, - and _ only), or untick it.
DnsPickTestTickedTip: Test only the servers you have ticked (among those shown) instead of every server in the list.
DnsPickTestTickedNone: Tick the servers you want to test first.
DnsPickSourceSaved: Showing only the servers you added: {0} (the list could not be loaded)
DnsPickNoList: The list has not been downloaded yet. Check your internet connection and press Refresh.
DnsPickSkippedFiles: {0} list file(s) need a newer MasselGUARD and were skipped.
DnsPickTestSkippedParam: {0} server(s) with an empty field were not tested.
